newsitem.title: ITALY: New trial ordered for Priebke - Italian agencies.
newsitem.headline: New trial ordered for Priebke - Italian agencies.

text.p: Italy's highest court of appeal on Tuesday ordered a new war crimes trial for former SS captain Erich Priebke, Italian news agencies reported.

The agencies ANSA and AGI reported that the Cassation Court had voided the verdict delivered by a military court on August 1 which found Priebke guilty of war crimes, but ordered him freed because the statute of limitations had run out.
The sentence had provoked angry protests and Priebke, 83, was re-arrested several hours later when Germany indicated it wanted to extradite him for a war crimes trial there.

The agencies said the Cassation Court reversed a ruling by a lower court which had rejected a challenge by the prosecution and civil plaintiffs to the impartiality of the chief trial judge, Agostino Quistelli.

They said the appeal court's ruling meant that Priebke, a German who lived openly in Argentina for 50 years after World War Two, would be retried for his role in the SS massacre of 335 Italian men and boys at the Ardeantine Caves near Rome in March 1944. Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.
